subject: LangLink SDK integration — edge-case walkthrough & tracing expectations
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: LangLink SDK integration — edge-case walkthrough & tracing expectations

Hi Evan / Anna,

Thanks again for the call last week — we had a few internal follow-ups and I wanted to propose a focused technical walkthrough to validate some edge cases before we schedule a wider sandbox. Specifically we'd like to cover:

- multi-model routing (how LangLink handles model fallbacks)
- tracing hooks (span shapes and OTLP export)
- LlamaIndex + LangLink runtime compatibility for long-context retrieval flows
- memory/KV cache eviction behaviors under sustained chat sessions

I attached a short spreadsheet with 4 representative scenarios (integration-scenarios.xlsx). Can you do a 45-minute walkthrough next week? Our suggested slots (PT): Tue 1/13 10:00–10:45, Wed 1/14 14:00–14:45. If those don't work please propose alternatives.

Goal for the session: a shared runbook of expectations (tracing fields, handshake for prompt instrumentation, recommended batching settings) so both teams can reproduce and validate in the sandbox environment. Vanessa from our partner engineering team will lead the demo. Marissa will follow on commercial fit / packaging.

Thanks — looking forward to locking a time.

Best,
Priyom
Sr. Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
Attachments: integration-scenarios.xlsx (Excel)
From: Evan Zhou <evan@langlink.ai>

Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: LangLink SDK integration — edge-case walkthrough & tracing expectations

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear agenda and the scenarios sheet, that helps. We can do Tue 1/13 at 10:00 PT. Quick questions to help us prepare: 

1) For tracing, do you expect OTLP with service.name=redwood-inference and spans that represent token-gen calls? We typically emit a span per request with attributes for model.name, prompt.hash, and duration_ms.
2) On the LlamaIndex side, are you expecting us to demonstrate a chunked-retrieval flow with streamed backfill? (we can mock the retrieval speed but want to ensure the span correlation works)
3) Any hard latency SLOs we should try to hit during the demo (p95 target)?

We'll bring one of our senior SDK engineers (Anna) and an infra engineer who can show the OTLP exporter config.

—Evan
Evan Zhou
Lead Integrations, LangLink Inc

Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: LangLink SDK integration — edge-case walkthrough & tracing expectations

Vanessa / Marissa — forwarding Evan's reply. Confirmed: Tue 1/13 10:00 PT.

Quick internal plan before the walkthrough: 
- Vanessa: lead demo (runtime routing + tracing correlation). Bring a short script to exercise fallback and streaming backfill.
- Marissa: be ready to walk commercial packaging options and an initial reciprocity framework if they want a co-marketing or sandbox credits arrangement.
- Priyom: own the runbook doc (link below) and capture open items.

Proposed walkthrough script (45m):
1) 5m intro + goals
2) 15m runtime demo (multi-model routing -> forced fallback -> cached response)
3) 10m tracing walkthrough (OTLP setup -> span examples -> attribute keys)
4) 10m LlamaIndex example (chunked retrieval -> span correlation)
5) 5m next steps + owners

Notes: emphasize that we need a deterministic set of span attribute keys so our console can correlate prompts -> traces (model.name, request.id, prompt.set_id). We should also validate event sizes (token counts) and KV cache behavior under >20 concurrent chat sessions.

Links: Redwood runbook draft — https://drive.google.com/redwood/langlink/runbook (I will attach a snapshot before the meeting)

If either of you want to add or pull someone in (runtime infra) let me know.

Priyom

Subject: Re: LangLink SDK integration — edge-case walkthrough & tracing expectations

Hi Evan / Anna — thanks, confirmed for Tue 1/13 10:00 PT. Attaching the current runbook snapshot (redwood-runbook-v1.docx) and the scenarios spreadsheet.

A few clarifications in response to your Qs: 
- Tracing: yes, OTLP is our preference. Service naming: service.name=redwood-inference is fine. We expect spans at request and token-gen levels where feasible; if token-level spans are too noisy we can accept request-level spans with token_count attribute. Required attributes: model.name, request.id, prompt.set_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, duration_ms.
- LlamaIndex: demonstrate a chunked retrieval + streaming backfill scenario; correlate retrieval spans to subsequent generation spans via request.id.
- Latency SLO: for the demo we won't gate on strict SLOs, but we should aim to keep p95 generation < 450ms for the 512-token synthetic test. If you can't meet that locally, capture the numbers so we can recommend optimizations.

Agenda link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/langlink/runbook
Attachments: redwood-runbook-v1.docx (Word), integration-scenarios.xlsx (Excel)

See you all on Tue.

Best,
Priyom
